captions.detailed: This 3D model consists of a two-part parametric filament spool designed for 3D printing. Each half features a flat circular flange (spool wall) with a central cylindrical hub extending upwards, allowing the two halves to mate together. One of the circular flanges has a small trapezoidal cutout near the outer edge for securing the filament end, and the hub walls feature small holes for filament entry.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric, two-part filament spool in OpenSCAD. The design should allow the user to adjust the spool width, outer wall diameter, wall thickness, central hole diameter, and filament diameter, producing two mating halves side-by-side with integrated filament securing slots.
captions.factory: The script defines parameters like spool_width, spool_walls_diameter, spool_walls_width, and spool_hole_diameter. It uses the cylinder primitive to construct the main flanges and cylindrical hubs for both halves. Boolean difference operations subtract the inner bore, create mating clearance offsets, drill small filament guide holes using rotated cylinders, and carve out a trapezoidal window in the flanges by subtracting a series of rotated cubes.
